Dutch open data

When is the greenest hour on the Dutch grid?

373 days of hourly grid data, from day-ahead prices to per-neighbor power flows. Right now the answer is usually 11:00–14:00, on 27% of the trailing 30 days. Every figure is open data, embedded in this page at build time.

Data received on 27 November 2026.

Why these hours: on a dynamic tariff, shifting flexible use such as charging or dishwashing into the window costs less and runs on the grid's most renewable-heavy hours. The window is thin this season: the full band opened on 8 of the last 30 days. Each bar counts how many of the trailing 30 days that hour met the green rule, counting any qualifying day, lone hours included. The bracket marks the recurring window: the hours that recur as a group most often, opening on 27% of days. A second, fainter bracket marks another recurring window between 03:00 and 05:00, opening on 23% of days. Snapshot-fresh as of 2026-11-27. All times Europe/Amsterdam.

The gas dayAvg day, last 30 days

What the average day does to gas-fired plants and prices: gas fills the gap between demand and clean supply, dips when clean supply is high, and rises again when demand picks up.

Between 04:00 and 19:00, average gas-fired output climbs from 5,096 MW to 6,715 MW, while the average price moves from 193.4 to 297.5 EUR/MWh.

Gas-fired production (MW)Day-ahead price (EUR/MWh, own scale)

The daylight renewables valleyAvg day, last 30 days

Distribution-connected renewables flood the grid in the sunny hours and prices sag with them.

Daylight renewables peak at 633 MW around 12:00, and the average day-ahead price bottoms at 193.4 EUR/MWh at 04:00, the heart of the green window.

Distribution-connected renewables (MW)Day-ahead price (EUR/MWh, own scale)

The evening peakAvg day, last 30 days

At the daily demand peak, prices follow and imports fill the gap.

Load peaks at 13,940 MW at 17:00 with prices at 320.4 EUR/MWh at 17:00, and over the trailing 30 days net imports covered 2.5% of Dutch load.

Load (MW)Day-ahead price (EUR/MWh, own scale)

The wind workhorseAvg day, last 30 days

Wind is the workhorse of the Dutch grid whenever it blows: high renewable share, low computed intensity, low prices.

Wind reaches 2,209 MW at 09:00, renewable share of generation peaks at 26.0% at 11:00, and computed intensity bottoms at 423 g CO2-eq/kWh (generation-mix basis).

Where power flowsLast 12 months

Cross-border physical flows (cbpf) between the Netherlands and its neighbors. Imports count up in teal, exports down in orange; the source's sign convention (imports positive, exports negative) is disclosed here.

Import and export per neighbor

ImportExport

Over the twelve months to 2026-11-27, the Netherlands imported 2.1 TWh and exported 19.3 TWh across all neighbors, a net export of -17.3 TWh. The busiest two-way border is Germany: 7.6 TWh in, 8.4 TWh out. Belgium takes the most: 14.8 TWh out. Flows are physical: power can transit the Dutch grid on its way elsewhere, so these figures describe where electricity crosses the border, not who traded it.

Disclaimer

What this atlas is and is not.

The Green Grid Atlas is an open-data story about the Dutch electricity grid, built from energy-charts.info (Fraunhofer ISE, CC BY 4.0; day-ahead prices from Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de, CC BY 4.0) and Open-Meteo weather (CC BY 4.0). It refreshes daily from a committed snapshot; it is snapshot-fresh, never live.

Computed carbon intensity uses the generation mix and does not attribute imports. The risk indicators are derived indicators, not a grid-security assessment. Nothing here is investment, switching, or grid-operations advice.

Method and sources

Every figure on this page traces to the committed snapshot, which records its source, license and retrieval date for each series.

Sourcing rule

Every figure on this page is fetched by scripts/backfill.mjs (once, full history) and scripts/snapshot.mjs (daily, 12:35 UTC) from the cited open data sources, politely paced (one request at a time, ≥ 31 s per endpoint, Retry-After honored), and stored with provenance in public/data/snapshot.json. Nothing statistical is hand-entered; all derived values are computed at render time or snapshot time from snapshot fields by the shared rule modules in src/grid. No API call ever happens from the client.

NL generation and load: sourcing basis

The Netherlands hourly generation per production type and actual total load come from the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform (document types A75 and A65, process type A16, bidding zone EIC 10YNL----------L), retrieved daily by the snapshot job and once for the full-history backfill. ENTSO-E timestamps are UTC interval starts; the pipeline converts them explicitly to Europe/Amsterdam local time through the same slot keying as every other series, and every build verifies the conversion hour-by-hour against the unchanged energy-charts price series. Renewable shares are computed from the per-type feeds: the renewable set is distribution-connected renewables (psrType B16 Solar plus B20 Other renewable), wind onshore, wind offshore, biomass, hydro run-of-river and poundage, hydro water reservoir, hydro pumped storage (generation side), geothermal and waste, over total generation for the share of generation and over actual load for the share of load.

Dutch solar and other distribution-connected renewables are reported by the TSO as a single upscaled estimate (ENTSO-E psrType B20 Other renewable plus B16 Solar); the site presents that aggregate rather than a decomposition, and the renewable share is unaffected because every component is renewable. The probe gate recorded an aggregate peak of 9.8 GW on the 2026-06-15 midday window, about 26.9% of the 36.46 GW daylight-connected fleet (energy-charts installed_power, latest record: solar AC plus onshore wind), an annualized aggregate of 39.2 TWh per year, and a midday-to-night mean ratio of 3.9 across the trailing year.

Fetch integrity: the platform serves each production type in two coexisting published blocks, so the fetch layer deduplicates per type by block completeness (the more complete block wins, a structural preference, never a value comparison) and verifies every accepted window against its load document: total generation energy must sit between 0.6 and 1.4 times the window's load energy (Dutch generation has been roughly 85–105% of load, per CBS), re-fetching the window fresh up to 3 times otherwise. These are fetch-integrity constants of the data pipeline, not display thresholds. An earlier probe run drew a defective platform variant of the same window; that run's figures are not shown here.

Historical note: the energy-charts NL solar series was defective (detected November 2026). It yielded about 0.48 TWh of solar per year against a 29.28 GW installed fleet (the same source's installed_power endpoint), while CBS reports 25.52 billion kWh of Dutch solar production in 2025 (provisional). Fixed in November 2026 by switching NL generation and load to ENTSO-E per-type data. The full probe report and the cross-zone solar audit are recorded in the pull request description.

Basis disclosure (verbatim)

Computed carbon intensity uses the generation mix: domestic production types times the emission-factor table, divided by load. Imports are not attributed: cross-border flows carry no fuel mix, so import-heavy hours show a lower computed intensity than the power actually consumed would cause. This limitation applies everywhere intensity is shown (the intensity layer label, the green window card captions, the coda).

The green window rule (verbatim)

The green window is computed from the trailing 30 days of hourly values (price and renewable share of generation), each hour independent. A green hour has price at or below the 30th percentile of the trailing price distribution AND renewable share at or above the 70th percentile of the trailing renewable-share distribution. A red hour is the exact inverse through the same code path: price at or above the 70th percentile AND renewable share at or below the 30th percentile. The rendered window is the hour interval (at least two contiguous wall-clock hours) that recurs most often as a whole: the number of trailing days on which every hour of the interval qualifies under the rule above. Ties prefer the longer interval, then the earliest start. Its frequency share is the share of trailing days on which the full interval qualifies. Hours qualifying outside the window still count in the frequency strip and the risk indicators individually. Percentiles use linear interpolation on the sorted hourly sample. Basis: renewable share of generation (NL generation mix); price is the NL day-ahead price. The strip can also mark one other recurring window: the strongest interval that qualifies on at least half as many days as the window and is separated from it by at least one hour. It is drawn fainter than the window and named with its opening share in the caption.

Constants: trailing 30 days, green price ≤ p30 / renewables ≥ p70, red price ≥ p70 / renewables ≤ p30. They live only in src/grid/green-window.ts and change only by editing that file; any change is stated in the PR description.

Risk indicator rules

  • Negative-price hours: Share of trailing-30-day hours with day-ahead price below 0 EUR/MWh. Watch at ≥ 1%, high at ≥ 5%.
  • Red-hour share: Share of trailing-30-day hours qualifying as red hours under the green window rule (price ≥ 70th percentile AND renewable share of generation ≤ 30th percentile, same code path as the green window). Watch at ≥ 20%, high at ≥ 35%.
  • Load covered by net imports: Over the trailing 30 days: Σ max(0, net physical import in GW × 1000) / Σ load in MW: the share of Dutch load covered by net imports (cross-border physical flows, imports positive). Watch at ≥ 25%, high at ≥ 40%.
  • Price spread (p90−p10): Trailing-30-day hourly price spread: 90th minus 10th percentile of day-ahead price, EUR/MWh. Watch at ≥ 150 EUR/MWh, high at ≥ 250 EUR/MWh.
  • Longest Dunkelflaute run: Longest consecutive run of hours in the trailing 90 days with wind onshore + wind offshore + distribution-connected renewables below 20% of load. Watch at ≥ 24 h, high at ≥ 48 h.

Indicators derived from open data; not a grid-security assessment..

DST rule (verbatim)

All grids render in Europe/Amsterdam local time. The two 23-hour and 25-hour days each year render their actual hour count (23 or 25 columns), with the missing spring-forward hour shown as an explicit gap cell and the doubled fall-back 02:00 shown as two labelled columns (02:00 +02:00 and 02:00 +01:00). Nothing is ever silently shifted.

Units

Prices EUR/MWh (day-ahead, NL bidding zone). Production, load, residual load MW. Cross-border physical flows GW, imports positive / exports negative. Renewable shares percent. Computed intensity g CO2-eq/kWh. Volumes TWh. Weather: wind speed 10 m km/h, shortwave radiation W/m², temperature 2 m °C. Timestamps are interval starts in Europe/Amsterdam with explicit UTC offset.

The atlas rhythm grids

The atlas card renders month-by-hour rhythm grids over the trailing window (20 November 2025 to 27 November 2026, 373 days): each cell is the mean of that local hour across all days of that calendar month present in the trailing window, computed at build time from the snapshot's trailing days. The slot-to-hour mapping uses the existing DST wall-hour sequence, so the 23-hour spring-forward day contributes no 02:00 sample and the 25-hour fall-back day contributes both of its 02:00 slots to the 02:00 cell (wall-hour collapse; nothing is silently shifted). Months are calendar months across the window, and the two edge months are partial, cut by the window's first and last day. Colour domains are the min and max of each grid's own cells, computed at build time: the price scale positions values by the square root of the domain position so spike hours do not wash out the normal range, the renewable-share scale is linear, and the legend ticks are rounded values computed from that domain.

Suppression and gap rendering

Missing or suppressed source values are stored as null and rendered as grey gap cells with a "no data" label, never as zero, never interpolated. The rhythm-grid colour scales span the min to max of each grid's own cells, computed at build time; the legend prints rounded tick values chosen from that domain.

Chart axes

Every bar chart carries one left y-axis computed at build time from its own series: zero sits at the baseline, the top tick is the series maximum rounded up to a human step from the 1, 2, 5 family, with three to five tick values, and the unit is stated once per axis (MW for the day profiles, GW for the flow timelines, TWh for the volume bars). The overlay line in the day profiles is scaled to its own maximum, so it deliberately does not share the bar axis; its exact values appear in the tooltip on hover, keyboard focus or tap.

Chart interaction

One shared tooltip (a single client component, components/chart-tooltip.tsx) follows the cursor over every chart and snaps to the nearest datum. On keyboard focus of a chart element the tooltip appears anchored to that element; on touch devices a tap positions it at the tapped datum and marks it active, a tap on another datum moves it, and a tap outside the chart or any scroll dismisses it. The tooltip is aria-hidden and visual only; every chart element keeps its own aria-label as the screen-reader channel. Hover and touch emphasis is stroke-only, so no interaction ever changes the layout.

AI disclosure

The “AI insight (Experimental)” captions are generated at snapshot time by Mistral (mistral-small-latest, temperature 0.2) from the same aggregates that power the visual, gated by SHA-256 context signatures, validated so every numeral comes from the context (numerals-only guidance, prose-ratio lint), capped at two calls per visual and sixteen per run, and hidden when generation fails. They render verbatim as static text; no AI call happens in the browser. Key lives only in the MISTRAL_API_KEY Actions secret.
